gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sun Gold Power's SGR-8K10E kit includes PV wiring for just one string (one 25 A PV breaker and one 50 ft PV extension cable set) even though its 8 kW inverter has two MPPT inputs. So all eight 450 W panels (30.08 V Vmp each) go in one series string of about 240.6 V Vmp, which stays under the inverter's 500 VDC open-circuit maximum, and the second MPPT input stays free for more panels later.
standout_why: I compared this against the Current Connected EG4 TinyHome kit page (a top result, opened 2026-11-10). It gives its own inverter's PV window (Fortress Solo 6.5K, 150–450 Vdc MPPT, 550 Vdc maximum) and the panel Voc/Vmp. It does not say how to wire the panels into strings or confirm battery-to-inverter communication, and it does not cover the Sun Gold Power kit at all. I tried the cited Renogy 1200W/2500W 48V cabin kit page (renogy.com/products/1200w-2500w-tiny-house-home-cabin-kit) but it returned HTTP 429, so I could not check its wording. Its stringing details apply to Renogy hardware in any case, not to this kit. I scored 2 rather than 3 because the finding that would have decided the set (splitting the panels 4+4 across both MPPTs drops below the MPPT voltage floor) depends on a 125–425 V MPPT range I could not open from a maker or manual page. That is listed under unsourced.
kit_items: inverter: Sun Gold Power 8 kW 48 V split-phase all-in-one inverter (120/240 V, 2 MPPT, 500 VDC maximum open-circuit). It is the inverter in the SGR-8K10E. The kit page says it supports up to 11,000 W of PV and talks to the batteries over RS485.

battery: 2 × Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2 V 100 Ah LiFePO4 server-rack batteries (10.24 kWh). They match the inverter's 48 V DC bus, and the kit page says both inverter and batteries support RS485. The kit includes a 250 A busbar and 2 × 2/0 AWG cable sets to join the two batteries.

solar panels: 8 × Sun Gold Power 450 W bifacial N-type panels (3,600 W total, 30.08 V Vmp each), with 8 sets of Z-brackets. One series string is 8 × 30.08 = 240.6 V Vmp, inside the inverter's 500 VDC open-circuit limit. The kit ships one 25 A PV breaker and one 50 ft PV extension set, which suits a single string.
DC protection and wiring: 200 A DC breaker, 25 A PV breaker and 2/0 AWG cables are all in the kit, so nothing has to come from another store. Racking beyond the Z-brackets is not listed.

findings.product: Sun Gold Power 8KW 48V Split Phase Solar Inverter
findings.label: Maximum PV open-circuit voltage
findings.note: Taken from the maker store's product text via storecheck search: 'Max.Voltage of Open Circuit : 500VDC', 2 MPPT, split-phase or 120 V single-phase, UL 1741 by ETL. Standalone price is $1,305.00. A direct page fetch returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Panel Vmp and single-string voltage
findings.value: 30.08 V per panel; 240.6 V for 8 in series
findings.note: Arithmetic: 8 × 30.08 V = 240.64 V. This is operating voltage (Vmp), not Voc. A cold-weather Voc check against the 500 V limit needs the panel Voc and its temperature coefficient (see unsourced). The manual filename on the page is SGN-450-BDG5. The page URL says '415-watts' but the title says 450 W.

findings.label: Battery-inverter communication
findings.note: Exact wording: 'The 48V inverter and 51.2V LiFePO4 batteries support RS485 communication'. The page does not name the cable, pinout or inverter battery-type setting.

findings.label: DC side hardware included
findings.value: 200 A DC breaker, 2 sets × 2/0 AWG cables, 250 A busbar, 8 sets Z-brackets
findings.note: The busbar joins the two SG48100P batteries. The SGR-8K10T (single SG48200T) and SGR-8K16P (PowerMax 314 Ah) variants list one cable set and no busbar.

unsourced: SGN-450-BDG5 panel Voc (a search snippet said 35.03 V), Isc (16.05 A) and Voc temperature coefficient (-0.28 %/K). The Solaris-shop datasheet PDF I fetched could not be read as text, the Solaris product page shows specs only as an image, and the maker's panel page returned HTTP 429. Without these I can't do the cold-weather Voc check (8 × Voc corrected for cold, against 500 VDC).

The 8 kW inverter's MPPT operating window (125–425 Vdc per search snippets) and maximum PV current per MPPT (22 A per snippet). I tried the maker's inverter page (HTTP 429), the SPH8-10KW manual PDF on the maker's Shopify CDN (could not read the text), manuals.plus (HTTP 403), offgridsource, offgridstores and kratopower (all HTTP 429). If 125 V is confirmed, a 4+4 split across both MPPTs (4 × 30.08 = 120.3 V Vmp) would fall below the MPPT floor, which would require the single 8-panel string.
Exact inverter model number for the kit (SPH8048P vs SPH8K48SP): the kit page only shows a manual filename 'SPH8-10KW'.
The RS485 cable, pinout and inverter battery-protocol setting for the SG48100P. They are not on the kit page, and the manual PDF could not be read.
The cited Renogy 1200W/2500W 48V cabin kit page returned HTTP 429, so I could not check its stringing or communication wording against this finding.
